citations.text: The study protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Tehran University of Medical Sciences.
The primary endpoints in this trial were a decrease in mortality, duration of hospitalisation and need for intensive care unit (ICU) admission.
Ethical approval: This project was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Tehran University of Medical Sciences [IR.TUMS.VCR.REC.1399.165].

5.1.reasoning: The paper names no trial registration, published protocol or statistical analysis plan with a date; the only document cited is an ethics approval, which fixes nothing about this outcome's measure or analysis. There is therefore no pre-specified plan to compare the reported mortality result against.

citations.text: The main outcome measures were vital signs, SpO2 levels, duration of hospitalisation, need for and length of intensive care unit admission, mortality rate and results of 30-day follow-up after discharge.

Differences in duration of hospitalisation, number of patients whose condition deteriorated and required ICU admission, length of ICU stay, mortality rate and results of 30-day follow-up after discharge were also evaluated as outcome measures.
There was one death ‏in the control group ‏and none in the case group; this difference was insignificant (P = 0.495).

5.2.reasoning: The methods list results of the 30-day follow-up after discharge as an outcome measure, yet no results for that follow-up are reported; only in-hospital deaths (0 vs 1, numerically favouring AZM) are given, and the paper does not explain the omission. With no registration or protocol it is unclear whether the results guided which measurement was shown.

citations.text: The χ2 test and Fisher's exact test were used to assess the statistical relationships between categorical variables.
The number needed to treat with a confidence interval (CI) of 95% was reported for requirement for ICU admission, need for intubation and mortality rate.
We also evaluated the effect size based on Hedges’ g because of the difference in the number of participants in each group.

5.3.reasoning: The mortality comparison could have been analysed in more than one way (Fisher's exact test, risk difference, NNT, effect size), and the paper cites no registration, protocol or analysis plan fixing which analysis was intended. With no such plan to hold the report against, the choice of analysis cannot be judged.
